description: CholeskyQR2 runs TWO potrf+trsm passes everywhere. A sibling proved both passes are load-bearing on shape 11's gapless rank-deficient basis, but the low-rank peel shapes 3/8/10/12 orthonormalize DOMINANT subspaces that may be better-conditioned (kappa small enough that one pass leaves orth under gate). Probe each low-rank shape's basis conditioning (cheap: the diagonal of the Cholesky factor R, or a Gram condition estimate already available) and route SINGLE-pass CholeskyQR (one potrf+trsm) where kappa^2 error clears the orth gate, keeping the 2nd pass only where conditioning needs it. Halves the potrf+trsm work on the shapes that qualify. Targets redundant-work (a 2nd orthonormalization pass on well-conditioned bases); keep the per-matrix residual gate + cuSOLVER fallback + orthogonality-edge calibration, route guarded per shape.

Gated off => hot path unchanged, geomean 27245.97us == parent 27237.04us (0.03%, noise). MEASURED conditioning + orth distribution on the 4 low-rank peel shapes (live custom_kernel on real generate_input): the R-diagonal condition estimate kd=max/min(diag chol) and orth after pass1(=1-pass) vs pass2(=2-pass), gate=80*n*eps. VERDICT: NO low-rank peel shape's 1-pass orth clears the gate on EITHER block -- both dominant and complement need 2 passes (identical to shape 11). nsys: CQR potrf+trsm is a real lever -- shape3 ~20pct (trsm 17.5+potrf 2.3), shape8 ~21pct, shape10 ~11pct, shape12 ~41pct (trsm 22.5+potrf 18.7) of shape cost. Per-shape baseline us: shape3=74332.5 shape8=80850.2 shape10=90791.5 shape12=29912.8. Fallback count 0 on all 4.

Geomean 27042-27031us vs parent 27237.04us = -0.74pct, reproducible (2 runs within 0.04pct), gate-clean, reseed-safe (16 shape/seed combos all valid, fallback 0 in 15/16). 39/39 valid, no 'stream', -O3.

MECHANISM (brief's design, built in _lr_cholesky_qr2): after CQR pass 1, compute per-matrix R-diagonal ratio kd=max/min(diag chol) (kappa(Q)~kd); route each matrix single-pass where the CholeskyQR 1-pass orth bound kd^2*n*eps < margin*(80*n*eps). Gather only the need-2 subset for pass 2 (gather-worth-it guard: full-batch 2nd pass when <max(8,B/16) skip). Per-matrix residual gate + cuSOLVER fallback backstops misjudgment. Wired ONLY into the complement's 2nd CQR (compl_pass2) at margin=1.0.

CONDITIONING + 1-vs-2-pass ORTH DISTRIBUTION (t1, measured live per shape, gate=80*n*eps):
- DOMINANT power CQR2 1-pass orth: shape3 2.885 / shape8 1.357 / shape10 1.377 / shape12 2.613, ALL 100pct over gate; 2-pass -> 3e-4..1.4e-2. kd(input)~194-257. Genuinely needs 2 passes (matches shape11). No single-pass here.
- COMPLEMENT is 4 CQR passes: compl_pass1(2) + reproject + compl_pass2(2). compl_pass1 1-pass orth 2.6-4.0 (100pct over) -> both passes load-bearing (t5 PROVED: compl_pass1=1 regressed +12.4pct geomean, shape12 +87pct). compl_pass2 pass0 (=3rd overall) orth already 6e-3..8.5e-2 with kd~1 for the majority (tail up to 57) -> its 2nd pass (4th overall) is REDUNDANT for the well-conditioned majority. THIS is the single-pass opportunity.
- Gate skip counts (margin=1.0): shape3 638/640, shape8 638/640, shape10 59/60, shape12 60/60 skip compl_pass2's 2nd pass with fallback=0.

WHY THE GATE WORKS ONLY ON compl_pass2: the kd^2*eps predictor is accurate only when the input is already near-orthonormal (post-reprojection). For compl_pass1/dominant (far-from-orthonormal inputs) the real 1-pass orth (2-4) is 1000x the kd^2*eps prediction, so gating them is unsafe (= t5 regression).

PER-SHAPE (gate-off t2 -> gate-on t6): shape3 74468->73127 (-1.8pct), shape8 80992->80031 (-1.2pct), shape10 90755->90510 (~noise, only 1/60 skips -- CQR is minor there, mega_eigh_clust is 66pct), shape12 30271->29043 (-4.1pct, all 60 skip, CQR is 41pct of the shape). nsys confirms batch_trsm_left instances shape3 30->27, shape8 26->24, shape12 58->48; potrf_syrk_nc shape12 51->42. Shape11 unchanged (its sign-DC uses _sign_dc_cqr, NOT _lr_cholesky_qr2 -- guardrail structurally satisfied).

OPEN DIRECTIONS (not closed): (1) margin sweep 1->16 all gate-clean but skip counts saturate at margin=1 (only +1-2 matrices at margin>=4) -- a margin>1 could be tried but gains look sub-noise. (2) The complement STILL runs compl_pass1's 2 full passes (n x nc trsm, the biggest CQR sub-cost on shape12 nc=640) -- conditioning-gating it is unsafe (t5), but a DIFFERENT reduction (e.g. a cheaper first-basis construction that needs fewer passes, or fusing reproject+CQR) is unexplored. (3) The dominant power CQR2's 2 passes (kd~200) are the other big trsm block on shapes 3/8/12 -- untouched here; a non-conditioning approach (e.g. blocked/shifted CQR that converges in fewer passes on ill-conditioned input) is open. (4) shape10 barely benefits (mega_eigh_clust dominates) -- its lever is the inner cluster solve, not CQR. (5) The gate's gather uses index_select/index_copy; a fused masked-CQR kernel could remove the gather sync for the mixed-skip shapes.
